references.description: Saved network configuration supports contextual baseline and legacy-protocol review. These references do not establish effective policy, exposure, compromise or framework compliance.
references.recommendation: Review the observed adapter, profile and explicit DNS policy settings against the approved network baseline and documented exceptions. Validate applicability and effective behavior separately; only authorized administrators may apply changes.
references.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
references.description: A local endpoint inventory supports reviewing unnecessary services. A non-loopback binding is review context, not proof that the service is unnecessary, reachable or noncompliant.
references.recommendation: Compare every binding with the approved service inventory and business need. Have authorized administrators remove unnecessary services and review host filtering; retain justified exceptions and reassess through a confirmed scan.

references.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
references.description: Remote Desktop configuration contributes context to secure remote access and configuration management. Enabling a needed host is not automatically a vulnerability. NLA is not MFA; these local observations prove neither network exposure, an attack nor compliance.
references.recommendation: Review the approved need for RDP, authentication, TLS, native encryption, credential handling and trusted connection files. Have an authorized administrator apply the reviewed policy. Validate access restrictions and MFA separately; reassess only through a confirmed read-only scan.

references.title: Encrypt Data on End-User Devices
references.description: CIS Controls v8.1 safeguard 3.6 addresses encryption of sensitive data on end-user devices. The Windows volume and two local criteria are a partial view; data classification, other volumes and the enterprise population are not assessed.
references.recommendation: Review sensitive-data scope and the approved device encryption standard. Have the authorized administrator address confirmed encryption or protection deviations after verifying recovery arrangements. Select algorithm and key length from approved policy and Microsoft guidance; this safeguard does not itself grade 128 versus 256 bits. Repeat the read-only assessment.

references.title: Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software
references.description: Authorized anti-malware and its approved configuration provide context for core Defender, PUA, cloud and tamper settings. These checks do not assess the complete safeguard.
references.recommendation: Confirm the authorized primary anti-malware product, review its approved configuration and any documented exceptions, then restore the reviewed protections through authorized administration and repeat the WinSec assessment.

references.title: Use Behavior-Based Anti-Malware Software
references.description: Behavior-based anti-malware capabilities and an approved configuration standard provide context for the behavior-monitoring rule.
references.recommendation: Confirm that behavior-based protection is required for this device, review temporary exceptions, and have the authorized administrator restore the approved behavior-monitoring configuration before repeating the read-only assessment.

references.title: Enable Anti-Exploitation Features
references.description: ASR vulnerable signed driver blocking is one anti-exploitation configuration. Existing driver loading and other exploit protections are not tested.
references.recommendation: Review the approved anti-exploitation baseline and application compatibility. Have the authorized administrator configure the specific vulnerable-driver ASR rule in Block mode, document exceptions and repeat the read-only scan. Do not enable all ASR rules indiscriminately.

references.title: Perform Automated Operating System Patch Management
references.description: CIS 7.3 covers automated OS patching across enterprise assets. Local automation configuration is only part of that process, not proof of installation or enterprise coverage.
references.recommendation: Have the administrator resolve the confirmed service or policy deviation and establish approved automatic patch deployment. Verify installation separately; repeat the read-only assessment.

references.title: Perform Automated Operating System Patch Management
references.description: CIS 7.3 addresses recurring OS patch deployment. WinSec compares one reviewed cumulative Windows baseline; its seven-day deadline is local policy, not a CIS requirement.
references.recommendation: Have the administrator verify the missing baseline, compatibility and maintenance arrangements, then complete approved deployment and any required restart. Review other applicable updates separately and reassess.

references.title: Ensure Authorized Software is Currently Supported
references.description: CIS 2.2 links software authorization to vendor support and documented exceptions. This Windows lifecycle check does not assess the complete software inventory or approve an exception.
references.recommendation: Review exact Windows edition, release and support arrangements with the administrator. Plan migration to a supported release, or document an authorized exception, compensating safeguards and accepted residual risk. An exception does not change this recorded lifecycle result.

references.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
references.description: Observed SMBv1 components and dependencies provide context for removing unnecessary services and features. Installation is not evidence of active connections, exploitation or complete compliance with safeguard 4.8.
references.recommendation: Confirm which legacy SMB dependencies are necessary, migrate them to supported protocols and have an authorized administrator remove unnecessary SMBv1 components. Document any accepted exception separately.

references.title: Implement and Manage a Firewall on End-User Devices
references.description: Host Firewall configuration contributes context to network filtering. Disabled profiles, permissive defaults and broad exceptions require review. Logging is complementary monitoring context. These observations do not prove compliance, reachability, exploitation or complete mitigation.
references.recommendation: Review the effective policy for Domain, Private and Public profiles, approved application and service exceptions, block precedence, and monitoring requirements. Have an authorized administrator apply the approved filtering policy; reassess through a confirmed read-only scan.
